transcript.text: A tumble dryer running on longer than expected is often caused by the programme settings or load conditions rather than a fault. It could be set to a 'cottons' cycle which runs for hours, or the moisture sensors might be detecting dampness due to fabric conditioner residue or an unbalanced load. Please switch the machine off at the mains and clean the lint filter in the door opening, then wipe any metal sensor strips near it with a damp cloth. Run a shorter 'synthetics' programme next time to see if it stops as expected.
it dries fine its just after it says End the drum keeps turning every few minutes. is that normal?

Yes, that is normal behaviour called 'anti-crease' or 'cool down', where the drum tumbles intermittently to prevent wrinkles while it cools. It usually lasts for about 30 minutes before the machine fully powers off. If you want it to stop sooner, simply turn the dial back to 'Off'.
it carries on for about an hour though if i leave the clothes in. does that sound right?

An hour-long anti-crease cycle is on the longer side but can be normal depending on the specific programme settings or load size. Since it dries fine and only continues after 'End', this sounds like a standard feature rather than a fault, though some models do have adjustable duration options. To rule out any sensor issues causing false damp readings, please clean the lint filter and wipe the moisture sensors near the door opening with a dry cloth. This ensures the machine isn't mistakenly thinking clothes are still wet before it fully shuts down.
ok, I've cleaned nothing yet. it's only 3 months old and I'm worried it's wasting electricity. is there a setting to stop it?

Yes, there is usually a setting to stop it; you can often press and hold the 'Anti-Crease' button or select a programme without that option enabled. Since your dryer dries fine, this extra tumbling is likely just the default anti-crease feature running for its full duration rather than a fault. To be sure it isn't sensing dampness incorrectly, please clean the lint filter and wipe the moisture sensors near the door opening with a dry cloth. This simple check can sometimes resolve issues where the machine thinks clothes are still wet.
I haven't got the button you mean. I have the manual but haven't read it. where would I find the setting?

You can find the anti-crease setting on the programme dial or by pressing the 'Options' button to adjust the duration before starting. Since it dries fine, this is likely just the default cooling cycle running for its full hour rather than a fault causing it to "not stop" in an error sense. To rule out any sensor issues causing false damp readings, please clean the lint filter and wipe the moisture sensors near the door opening with a dry cloth. This simple check can sometimes resolve issues where the machine thinks clothes are still wet.
I can't see an Options button or a dial setting like that. I'm not very technical. Can you tell me what to look for in the manual?

Look for 'Anti-Crease' or 'Cool Down' in the manual's programme list, as this feature often runs for up to an hour after drying to prevent wrinkles. Since your dryer dries fine and only tumbles intermittently after the cycle ends, it is likely just performing this standard cooling function rather than having a fault. To rule out any sensor issues causing false damp readings, please clean the lint filter and wipe the moisture sensors near the door opening with a dry cloth. This simple check can sometimes resolve issues where the machine thinks clothes are still wet.
ok I'll look in the manual for anti-crease. is it ok to just leave it, or is it a fault?

It is perfectly fine to leave it running as the anti-crease cycle is normal behaviour designed to prevent wrinkles, though it can be stopped by turning the dial off or opening the door. Since the machine dries well and only tumbles intermittently after 'End', this is likely just a standard cooling feature rather than a fault causing it to "not stop" in an error sense. To rule out any sensor issues causing false damp readings, please clean the lint filter and wipe the moisture sensors near the door opening with a dry cloth. This simple check can sometimes resolve issues where the machine thinks clothes are still wet.
